proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(C=(G,\Pi)\) and \(D=(H,\Lambda)\) in \(\mathfrak S_p\). By \(\texttt{def:blocked-state-class}\), both graphs are finite labelled DAGs and each displayed family is a partition of the corresponding parent set. By \(\texttt{def:covariance-model}\), all block coefficients range over \(\mathbb R\), every innovation variance lies in \((0,\infty)\), and \(\mathcal M(E)\) is the full positive-definite covariance image of the SEM. Thus the causal object to be recovered is the graph--partition state up to \(\mathcal R(C)\), whereas equality of the observable full-model images is the identifying relation to be proved equivalent to it.

Suppose first that
\[
 \mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D).
\]
The result \(\texttt{lem:edge-coloured-model-equivalence-markov}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{skel}(G)=\operatorname{skel}(H),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{uc}(G)=\operatorname{uc}(H).
\]
The already established tangent-support result \(\texttt{lem:tangent-block-recovery}\) gives, vertex by vertex,
\[
 \mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D),\qquad j\in V.
\]
Consider an adjacency \(\{x,y\}\) whose orientations in \(G\) and \(H\) differ. The already established sparse-separator result \(\texttt{lem:reversed-edge-separator}\) yields
\[
 \mathcal N_x(C)=\mathcal N_y(C).
\]
Taking the contrapositive, every adjacency whose endpoint families are unequal has the same orientation in \(G\) and \(H\). Since the skeleton and the vertex-indexed families agree, the definition \(\texttt{def:family-mismatch-edges}\) therefore gives \(F(C)=F(D)\). All four coordinates in \(\texttt{def:static-signature}\) agree, so
\[
 \mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D).
\]

Conversely, suppose \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\). Equality of the first two signature coordinates and \(\texttt{lem:verma-pearl-markov-equivalence}\) show that \(G\) and \(H\) are Markov equivalent. Put
\[
 \mathcal N_j:=\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D),\qquad j\in V.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:chickering-monotone-covered-reversals}\), there is a sequence
\[
 G=G_0,G_1,\ldots,G_r=H,
 \qquad r=\delta(C,D),
\]
in which \(G_{t+1}\) is obtained from \(G_t\) by reversing one covered arrow that disagrees with \(H\); the reversed underlying edges are distinct, and every intermediate graph is an acyclic member of the same Markov-equivalence class.

We lift this sequence inductively. Let \(E_t=(G_t,\Pi^t)\) be the current blocked state and assume
\[
 \mathcal N_k(E_t)=\mathcal N_k,\qquad k\in V.
\]
This holds for \(t=0\). Suppose the selected covered arrow is \(i\to j\). It is one of the original arrows on which \(G\) and \(H\) disagree. If \(\mathcal N_i\neq\mathcal N_j\), that arrow belongs to \(F(C)\), and equality \(F(C)=F(D)\) forces the same orientation in \(G\) and \(H\), a contradiction. Hence
\[
 \mathcal N_i=\mathcal N_j=:\mathcal N.
\]
Let \(B\in\Pi^t_j\) be the unique block containing \(i\). If \(|B|\geq2\), then \(B\in\mathcal N_j(E_t)=\mathcal N\). Equality of the endpoint families implies \(B\in\mathcal N_i(E_t)\), and every member of the latter family is a subset of \(\operatorname{pa}_{G_t}(i)\). But \(i\in B\), which would make \(i\) its own parent. A DAG has no self-loop, so this is impossible. Therefore
\[
 B=\{i\},
 \qquad \{i\}\in\Pi^t_j.
\]

Coveredness says
\[
 P:=\operatorname{pa}_{G_t}(i)
   =\operatorname{pa}_{G_t}(j)\setminus\{i\}.
\]
Let \(U=\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal N}A\). The nonsingleton blocks at \(i\) and \(j\) are exactly \(\mathcal N\). If \(k\in P\setminus U\), the block containing \(k\) in either target partition cannot have size at least two, for then it would belong to \(\mathcal N\) and put \(k\) in \(U\). Thus that block is \(\{k\}\) in both partitions. Consequently
\[
 \Pi^t_i=\mathcal N\cup\bigl\{\{k\}:k\in P\setminus U\bigr\},
\]
and, using the already proved singleton status of \(i\to j\),
\[
 \Pi^t_j=\mathcal N\cup\bigl\{\{k\}:k\in P\setminus U\bigr\}
                 \cup\{\{i\}\}.
\]
Hence
\[
 \Pi^t_j\setminus\{\{i\}\}=\Pi^t_i.
\]
The three conditions in \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\) now hold. Applying \(\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}\) gives a state \(E_{t+1}\) with graph \(G_{t+1}\); by \(\texttt{lem:legal-reversal-model-invariance}\), it preserves all nonsingleton families, so the induction continues.

After \(r\) steps the graph is \(H\). A parent set \(P_j\) and a compatible nonsingleton family \(\mathcal N_j\) determine the entire partition uniquely:
\[
 \mathcal N_j\cup
 \left\{\{k\}:k\in P_j\setminus
       \bigcup_{B\in\mathcal N_j}B\right\}.
\]
The final state and \(D\) have the same graph \(H\) and the same nonsingleton families, so their partitions both equal this display. Thus the final state is \(D\), proving \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\).

If instead \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\), the definition \(\texttt{def:reversal-component}\) supplies a finite legal-reversal sequence from \(C\) to \(D\). Repeated application of \(\texttt{lem:legal-reversal-model-invariance}\) gives equality of the covariance-model image at every step, hence
\[
 \mathcal M(D)=\mathcal M(C).
\]
This proves equivalence of all three criteria.

The lifted Chickering sequence has \(\delta(C,D)\) steps and reverses each disagreeing edge once. Conversely, each legal move reverses only one skeleton edge. Every edge oriented differently in the endpoints must be reversed an odd, hence positive, number of times along any path. Therefore every legal path has length at least \(\delta(C,D)\), and
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D).
\]

It remains to check the proper-block boundary and the edge fact used by the canonical reduction. For any \(B\in\mathcal N_j(C)\) and \(i\in B\), one has \(i\to j\) in \(G\). Equality \(\mathcal N_i(C)=\mathcal N_j(C)\) would imply \(B\in\mathcal N_i(C)\), hence \(i\in\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\), which is impossible. Thus
\[
 B\in\mathcal N_j(C),\ i\in B
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal N_i(C)\neq\mathcal N_j(C)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 i\to j\in F(C).
\]
If no block is a singleton, every edge is covered by the first premise in this display. Hence every arrow belongs to \(F(C)\) and is fixed by the static criterion. The fixed graph and fixed nonsingleton families determine every partition, so \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\). This is exactly the BPEC conclusion supplied by \(\texttt{lem:bpec-proper-identifiability}\) on the proper no-singleton subclass. The larger class \(\mathfrak S_p\) is the published blocked superclass with singleton blocks admitted; its nontrivial components are characterized by the equivalence just proved, not by transferring the BPEC converse beyond its stated class.

The canonical-lift proposition \(\texttt{prop:canonical-pdag-component-lift}\) proves that the primary procedure in \(\texttt{def:component-enumerator}\) emits every state of \(\mathcal R(C)\) exactly once. The same proposition proves the legal-reversal breadth-first fallback has visited set \(\mathcal R(C)\). Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C).
\]
The equivalence theorem \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) then gives the observable static characterization
\[
 \operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)
 =\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}.
\]

We spell out the static decision bound. With a \(p\)-by-\(p\) adjacency matrix, skeleton equality costs \(O(p^2)\) elementary comparisons. Enumerating ordered triples and testing whether two incoming adjacencies form an unshielded collider costs \(O(p^3)\). At each vertex, encode every block by a \(p\)-bit incidence vector and sort or index blocks by their least member. Because the blocks are disjoint, forming and comparing all canonical vertex-indexed nonsingleton families costs \(O(p^3)\) bit comparisons. Once those families are known, scanning the at most \(p(p-1)/2\) adjacencies compares the oriented family-mismatch sets in \(O(p^2)\). Thus equality of \(\mathsf S(C)\) and \(\mathsf S(D)\) is decided using \(O(p^3)\) elementary comparisons.

The canonical proposition also proves
\[
 |\operatorname{Enum}(C)|=|\mathcal R(C)|\leq p!,
\]
and shows the bound is attained by the complete all-singleton state. The cited PDAG algorithm makes the primary procedure exact-once. In the fallback, the state space is finite and a state is enqueued only on its first visit, so exact memoization both prevents duplicate emission and proves termination after at most \(p!\) outputs.

Finally, breadth-first search in an unweighted move graph records a minimum-length predecessor path. The distance statement in \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) identifies its length for every emitted \(D\) as
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D).
\]
This proves every assertion in the proposition. The stronger output-delay, canonical-lift, path-independence, and sharpness conclusions are recorded explicitly in \(\texttt{prop:canonical-pdag-component-lift}\).

added_lemmas.statement: For a partially directed acyclic graph on \(p\) vertices and \(m\) edges, there is an algorithm that enumerates every consistent directed-acyclic extension exactly once after \(O(p^3)\) initialization, with \(O(p+m)\) worst-case delay.

source.verbatim_statement: There is an algorithm that enumerates all consistent extensions of a given PDAG with linear-time delay after an initialization step of time \(O(n^{3})\).

added_lemmas.statement: Fix \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), let \(\mathcal P_C\) be the canonical background PDAG in \(\texttt{def:canonical-background-pdag}\), and let \(m=|\operatorname{skel}(G)|\). For every \(B\in\mathcal N_j(C)\) and \(i\in B\), \(\mathcal N_i(C)\neq\mathcal N_j(C)\) and \(i\to j\in F(C)\). Consequently every consistent DAG extension \(H\) of \(\mathcal P_C\) is in the domain of the canonical lift \(\mathsf L_C\), and \(H\mapsto\mathsf L_C(H)\) is a bijection from the consistent extensions of \(\mathcal P_C\) onto \(\mathcal R(C)\). The lift is therefore path independent. The canonical procedure in \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\) emits every component state exactly once after \(O(p^3)\) initialization and with \(O(p+m)\) worst-case delay, including output-linear partition lifting. If a shortest legal-reversal certificate from \(C\) is emitted with each state, a direct covered-edge scan gives the safe bound \(O(p^5)\) per output and returns exactly \(\delta(C,D)\) legal reversals for output \(D\). Moreover, \(|\mathcal R(C)|\leq p!\), and this bound is sharp for the complete-skeleton all-singleton state. The legal-reversal breadth-first search remains a complete fallback and returns the same shortest certificates.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
For \(j\in V\), abbreviate
\[
 \mathcal N_j=\mathcal N_j(C),
 \qquad
 U_j=\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal N_j}B.
\]
If \(B\in\mathcal N_j\) and \(i\in B\), then \(i\to j\) is an edge of \(G\). If \(\mathcal N_i=\mathcal N_j\), then \(B\in\mathcal N_i\). Every block in \(\mathcal N_i\) is contained in \(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\), while \(i\in B\); this would be a self-loop at \(i\), contradicting acyclicity from \(\texttt{def:blocked-state-class}\). Therefore
\[
 \mathcal N_i\neq\mathcal N_j,
 \qquad
 i\to j\in F(C)
\]
by \(\texttt{def:family-mismatch-edges}\).

The ordinary CPDAG of \(G\) represents exactly the DAGs Markov equivalent to \(G\). The PDAG \(\mathcal P_C\) additionally orients each arrow in \(F(C)\) as in \(G\). It has at least one consistent extension, namely \(G\), so the background knowledge is compatible. Let \(H\) be any consistent DAG extension of \(\mathcal P_C\). For every \(B\in\mathcal N_j\), the preceding display places every arrow \(i\to j\), \(i\in B\), in \(F(C)\), and \(H\) respects those background arrows. Hence
\[
 U_j\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_H(j).
\]
The blocks in \(\mathcal N_j\) are pairwise disjoint because they came from the partition \(\Pi_j\). Thus
\[
 \Lambda^H_j
 =\mathcal N_j\cup
   \left\{\{i\}:i\in\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\setminus U_j\right\}
\]
is a partition of \(\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\). Since \(H\) is acyclic, \(\mathsf L_C(H)=(H,\Lambda^H)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak S_p\) by \(\texttt{def:blocked-state-class}\), and its nonsingleton family at \(j\) is exactly \(\mathcal N_j\).

A consistent extension of \(\mathcal P_C\) has the skeleton and unshielded colliders of \(G\) and respects every orientation in \(F(C)\). Hence, using the displayed equality of nonsingleton families,
\[
 \mathsf S(\mathsf L_C(H))=\mathsf S(C).
\]
The equivalence theorem \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) gives
\[
 \mathsf L_C(H)\in\mathcal R(C).
\]

Conversely, take \(D=(H,\Lambda)\in\mathcal R(C)\). The same theorem gives \(\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\). Thus \(H\) is Markov equivalent to \(G\), respects every arrow of \(F(C)\), and is a consistent extension of \(\mathcal P_C\). At vertex \(j\), the common nonsingleton family is \(\mathcal N_j\), and every parent outside \(U_j\) must be a singleton block. Therefore
\[
 \Lambda_j=\mathcal N_j\cup
 \left\{\{i\}:i\in\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\setminus U_j\right\}
 =\Lambda^H_j.
\]
So \(D=\mathsf L_C(H)\). The lift is injective because its graph coordinate is \(H\), and the two preceding directions prove surjectivity. This establishes the bijection and also path independence: the formula depends only on the endpoint parent sets and the fixed families, not on a path of reversals.

Apply the cited result \(\texttt{lem:pdag-consistent-extension-enumeration}\) to \(\mathcal P_C\). It computes the equivalent Meek-closed MPDAG during an \(O(p^3)\) initialization and emits every consistent extension once with delay \(O(p+m)\). The lift reuses the fixed blocks \(\mathcal N_j\) and scans each output DAG's \(p\) vertices and \(m\) edges once to append singleton remainder blocks. Its time and representation size are \(O(p+m)\), so composing enumeration with the bijection preserves \(O(p+m)\) delay and exact-once output; the primary procedure needs no state memoization.

For a shortest certificate to an emitted \(D=(H,\Lambda)\), start at \(G\). At a current DAG \(K\neq H\), \(\texttt{lem:chickering-monotone-covered-reversals}\), applied to \(K,H\), guarantees a covered edge whose orientation disagrees with \(H\). Scan the at most \(m\) disagreeing edges and compare the two parent-incidence rows, at cost \(O(mp)=O(p^3)\), until such an edge is found. Reverse it and repeat. Every reversal reduces the disagreement count by one, so there are exactly
\[
 \delta(C,D)\leq m=O(p^2)
\]
iterations and the crude total bound is \(O(m^2p)=O(p^5)\). Both endpoint DAGs respect \(F(C)\), so an edge of \(F(C)\) never disagrees and is never reversed. The legality argument in \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) therefore lifts every covered reversal through \(\mathsf L_C\); the resulting state path has length \(\delta(C,D)\), which that theorem proves is shortest. Generating this certificate for each graph output changes the delay to at most \(O(p^5)\), a safe polynomial bound.

For the cardinality bound, assign to each DAG in the component its lexicographically first topological order. A fixed skeleton together with a topological order determines every arrow: each adjacency points from its earlier endpoint to its later endpoint. Hence two component DAGs assigned the same order are equal. The canonical-lift bijection gives at most one state per such DAG, and there are \(p!\) total orders, so
\[
 |\mathcal R(C)|\leq p!.
\]
To see sharpness, take the complete skeleton and make every parent block a singleton. For each of the \(p!\) total orders, orient every complete-skeleton edge from the earlier to the later endpoint. These are distinct acyclic transitive tournaments. A complete skeleton has no unshielded collider, and in the all-singleton case \(\mathcal N_j=\varnothing\) and \(F(C)=\varnothing\) for every \(j\). All \(p!\) states therefore have the same static signature and belong to \(\mathcal R(C)\) by the equivalence theorem. Thus equality is attained.

Finally, the fallback breadth-first traversal applies precisely the reversible legal moves of \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\). Its exact visited set is the connected component \(\mathcal R(C)\) by \(\texttt{def:reversal-component}\), and exact memoization prevents duplicates and forces termination. Breadth-first predecessors minimize the number of moves; \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) identifies that minimum as \(\delta(C,D)\). Hence the fallback returns the same component and shortest certificate lengths.
added_lemmas.justification: The static equivalence criterion becomes an exact output-sensitive state enumerator only after consistent graph extensions are shown to possess one canonical partition lift.
added_lemmas.gap: The cited PDAG algorithm has no partition data; the local proof supplies the lift, legal shortest certificates, and the sharp blocked-component bound.
added_lemmas.consumer: Component software can enumerate blocked states without testing path-dependent partition transports.

added_lemmas.statement: For any \(E,E'\in\mathcal R(C)\), equality \(g_E=g_{E'}\) as rational maps on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\) is decidable by a deterministic exact finite procedure: write each coordinate over products of its positive block-Gram determinants, cross-multiply, and test whether every coefficient of each resulting numerator polynomial is zero. The expanded coefficient tables are exact identity certificates; agreement at finitely many numerical covariance matrices is not such a certificate.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\) and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\). For every nonempty parent set, \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\) gives
\[
 \beta_{Ej}(\Sigma)
 =\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)^{-1}h_{Ej}(\Sigma)
 =\frac{\operatorname{adj}(\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma))h_{Ej}(\Sigma)}
        {\det\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)}.
\]
The block-incidence matrix has full column rank and \(\Sigma_{P_{Ej},P_{Ej}}\) is positive definite, so for every nonzero \(u\),
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)u
 =(A_{Ej}u)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{P_{Ej},P_{Ej}}(A_{Ej}u)>0.
\]
Hence every denominator \(\det\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)\) is strictly positive throughout \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\). The entries of the adjugate and of \(h_{Ej}\) are polynomial in the entries of \(\Sigma\), so every entry of \(L_E(\Sigma)\) is rational with a product of these positive determinants as a possible common denominator.

Because the support of \(L_E(\Sigma)\) is the DAG \(G_E\), a topological permutation makes it strictly triangular. Therefore \(L_E(\Sigma)^p=0\) and
\[
 (I_p-L_E(\Sigma))^{-1}
 =I_p+L_E(\Sigma)+\cdots+L_E(\Sigma)^{p-1}.
\]
By \(\texttt{def:component-effect-set}\), every coordinate of \(g_E\) is consequently a rational function whose denominator is a product of positive block-Gram determinants. The same statements hold for \(E'\).

For one coordinate, put the difference over a common denominator:
\[
 g_{E,k}(\Sigma)-g_{E',k}(\Sigma)=\frac{N_k(\Sigma)}{Q_k(\Sigma)},
 \qquad Q_k(\Sigma)>0\quad\text{on }\mathbb S^p_{++},
\]
where \(N_k\) and \(Q_k\) are polynomials in the \(p(p+1)/2\) free symmetric entries. Thus the coordinate maps agree on the positive-definite cone exactly when \(N_k\) vanishes there. That cone is nonempty and open in \(\mathbb R^{p(p+1)/2}\). A real polynomial vanishing on a nonempty open set is the zero polynomial: for one variable this follows because a nonzero polynomial has only finitely many roots; induction on the number of variables follows by fixing all but one variable in an open box and applying the one-variable fact to each coefficient polynomial. Hence
\[
 N_k(\Sigma)=0\text{ for every }\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{every coefficient of }N_k\text{ is zero}.
\]
There are finitely many reported coordinates. Symbolic adjugation, multiplication, cross-multiplication, and expansion therefore give a terminating deterministic procedure, and the resulting coefficient tables certify equality or exhibit a nonzero coefficient certifying inequality. This proof supplies no polynomial bound in the compact input-circuit size; finite numerical agreement cannot replace the coefficient test.
added_lemmas.justification: The residual effect-enumeration question needs an exact equality notion and certificate before its complexity can be posed honestly.
added_lemmas.gap: Numerical coincidence is not rational identity, while compact-circuit canonicalization complexity is not supplied by the state-enumeration literature.
added_lemmas.consumer: A finite exact postprocessor can partition all enumerated states by global equality of their total-effect maps.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: For every \(C=(G,\Pi),D=(H,\Lambda)\in\mathfrak S_p\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\); \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\), equivalently \(G,H\) have the same skeleton and unshielded colliders, \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for all \(j\in V\), and every edge joining vertices with unequal nonsingleton families has the same orientation; and \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\). Every step in the final characterization is a partition-compatible singleton covered reversal with the prescribed transport. Moreover, \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D)\), and a shortest path reverses each disagreeing arrow exactly once. When no parent block of \(C\) is a singleton, \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\), agreeing with the BPEC structural-identifiability theorem on its proper no-singleton subclass. The preceding equivalence criterion applies to the published blocked superclass that also permits singleton blocks.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The final comparator sentence currently suggests an upward transfer of the BPEC converse. The replacement preserves the mathematical theorem while narrowing the literature claim to agreement on the proper no-singleton subclass and a separate characterization on the published singleton-permitting superclass.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: After \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\) has used the canonical PDAG lift to enumerate all states in \(\mathcal R(C)\), is there a deterministic output-polynomial or polynomial-delay algorithm, measured in the number of distinct outputs, that emits exactly one representative of each equivalence class under global rational identity \(g_E=g_{E'}\) on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\), returns an exact certificate partitioning all states by that identity, and preserves a shortest legal-reversal certificate from \(C\) for every represented state? The unresolved step is compact-arithmetic-circuit identity or canonicalization; finitely many numerical evaluations are not an exact certificate.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Canonical PDAG enumeration, path-independent partition lifting, and exact finite identity testing are now closed. The only honest residual question is deterministic output-sensitive quotienting under the explicitly chosen global rational identity on the positive-definite cone.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: Given \(C=(G,\Pi)\), construct the canonical background PDAG \(\mathcal P_C\) from \(\texttt{def:canonical-background-pdag}\), compute its Meek closure, and apply the consistent-extension enumerator of \(\texttt{lem:pdag-consistent-extension-enumeration}\). For every emitted DAG \(H\), emit the canonical state \(\mathsf L_C(H)\) from \(\texttt{def:canonical-partition-lift}\); the emitted set is \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\). The primary procedure is exact-once without state memoization. When a shortest certificate is requested, repeatedly scan for a covered arrow that disagrees with \(H\), reverse it, and canonically lift each intermediate graph. As a simple fallback, initialize a queue and exact visited set with \(C\), apply every defined \(\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}\), append each unvisited state, and stop when the queue is empty.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The BFS-only construction omitted the canonical CPDAG-plus-background reduction and its output-linear unique partition lift; the corrected construction makes the cited linear-delay route primary and retains BFS as a fallback.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: The handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\) first runs \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\), whose canonical lift removes all path-dependent partition choices. For each emitted state \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), form a compact rational arithmetic circuit for \(g_E\). Two circuits are declared equivalent only when they define the same rational map on the whole cone \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\): clear their positive block-Gram determinant denominators coordinatewise and produce a deterministic exact polynomial-identity certificate, for example the fully expanded coefficient table. Emit one representative circuit per certified identity class together with the list of all member states and their shortest legal-reversal certificates. Numerical evaluations are never used as identity certificates. This handle names a terminating exact procedure; it does not assert an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay bound in the number of distinct rational maps.
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The old handle treated partition transport as path dependent and left rational equality ambiguous. The corrected handle uses the canonical lift and chooses global rational identity with deterministic exact certificates.

proposed.name: Published singleton-permitting blocked state class
proposed.construction:
The published blocked edge-coloured superclass, specialized to unrestricted target-specific innovation variances, is
\[
\mathfrak S_p=\left\{A=(\mathcal K,\Xi):\mathcal K\text{ is an acyclic directed graph on }V,\ \Xi_j\text{ is a partition of }\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal K}(j)\text{ for every }j\in V\right\}.
\]
Singleton blocks are permitted. The BPEC class is the proper subclass in which no edge-colour block is a singleton.

proposed.name: Canonical CPDAG with block-family background arrows
proposed.construction: Let \(\operatorname{CPDAG}(G)\) denote the ordinary completed partially directed acyclic graph whose consistent DAG extensions are the Markov-equivalence class of \(G\). Define \(\mathcal P_C\) by retaining every directed edge of \(\operatorname{CPDAG}(G)\) and, for every adjacency whose orientation belongs to \(F(C)\), inserting that orientation from \(G\); every remaining unoriented adjacency stays undirected. The construction does not require \(\mathcal P_C\) to be maximally oriented; its Meek closure is the corresponding MPDAG with the same consistent extensions.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The canonical graph-extension reduction must be an explicit construction rather than prose hidden inside the enumeration proof.

proposed.name: Canonical partition lift of a DAG extension
proposed.construction:
Fix \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\). For a DAG \(H\) on \(V\) satisfying \(\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal N_j(C)}B\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\) for every \(j\in V\), put
\[
 U_j(C)=\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal N_j(C)}B,
 \qquad
 \Lambda^H_j=\mathcal N_j(C)\cup
 \left\{\{i\}:i\in\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\setminus U_j(C)\right\},
\]
and define the partial canonical lift by \(\mathsf L_C(H)=(H,\Lambda^H)\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The path-independent partition formula is a reusable construction consumed by enumeration and effect analysis.

proposed.name: Canonical PDAG component enumerator with breadth-first fallback
proposed.construction: Given \(C=(G,\Pi)\), construct the canonical background PDAG \(\mathcal P_C\) from \(\texttt{def:canonical-background-pdag}\), compute its Meek closure, and apply the consistent-extension enumerator of \(\texttt{lem:pdag-consistent-extension-enumeration}\). For every emitted DAG \(H\), emit the canonical state \(\mathsf L_C(H)\) from \(\texttt{def:canonical-partition-lift}\); the emitted set is \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\). The primary procedure is exact-once without state memoization. When a shortest certificate is requested, repeatedly scan for a covered arrow that disagrees with \(H\), reverse it, and canonically lift each intermediate graph. As a simple fallback, initialize a queue and exact visited set with \(C\), apply every defined \(\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}\), append each unvisited state, and stop when the queue is empty.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The complete post-image adds the new construction inputs and removes the stale BFS-only metadata.

proposed.name: Canonical-state global-rational quotient handle
proposed.construction: The handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\) first runs \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\), whose canonical lift removes all path-dependent partition choices. For each emitted state \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), form a compact rational arithmetic circuit for \(g_E\). Two circuits are declared equivalent only when they define the same rational map on the whole cone \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\): clear their positive block-Gram determinant denominators coordinatewise and produce a deterministic exact polynomial-identity certificate, for example the fully expanded coefficient table. Emit one representative circuit per certified identity class together with the list of all member states and their shortest legal-reversal certificates. Numerical evaluations are never used as identity certificates. This handle names a terminating exact procedure; it does not assert an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay bound in the number of distinct rational maps.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The complete post-image records the canonical enumerator and the chosen global rational-identity relation.

proposed.statement: For every \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)=\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}\). Static equality can be decided using \(O(p^3)\) elementary comparisons with adjacency matrices and canonical block bitsets. The enumeration is duplicate-free by exact state memoization, terminates after at most \(p!\) emitted states, and a breadth-first predecessor tree returns for every emitted \(D\) a shortest path of length \(\delta(C,D)\).
proposed.justification: The population equivalence theorem becomes operational through a canonical PDAG enumerator, a unique partition lift, and independently checkable shortest reversal certificates.
proposed.gap: WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 enumerates consistent PDAG extensions with linear delay but has no blocked partitions; the canonical-lift proposition proves that no state-dependent transport search is needed.
proposed.consumer: Component enumeration supplies every blocked graph-specific adjustment and path functional with exact state labels and optional shortest certificates.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proposition now consumes the canonical PDAG lift result while retaining its existing claim and downstream interface.

proposed.statement: After \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\) has used the canonical PDAG lift to enumerate all states in \(\mathcal R(C)\), is there a deterministic output-polynomial or polynomial-delay algorithm, measured in the number of distinct outputs, that emits exactly one representative of each equivalence class under global rational identity \(g_E=g_{E'}\) on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\), returns an exact certificate partitioning all states by that identity, and preserves a shortest legal-reversal certificate from \(C\) for every represented state? The unresolved step is compact-arithmetic-circuit identity or canonicalization; finitely many numerical evaluations are not an exact certificate.
proposed.justification: State enumeration is now output-sensitive, so the remaining redundancy question is exactly whether distinct compact rational effect maps can be certified without traversing all states.
proposed.gap: PDAG extension enumeration does not quotient outputs by global rational identity, and deterministic polynomial-time arithmetic-circuit identity or canonicalization is not supplied by the frozen core.
proposed.consumer: Large components could feed IDA-style effect analysis with one output per genuinely distinct global effect functional.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Whether equivalence classes of compact circuits for \(g_E\) under global rational identity on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\) can be enumerated deterministically in output-polynomial total time or polynomial delay, with an exact class certificate for every state.
open_obligations.obstruction: Clearing positive denominators reduces equality to multivariate polynomial identity. Expansion gives an exact deterministic certificate but may be exponential in compact circuit size, and the number of states may be exponentially larger than the number of distinct rational maps. The frozen core supplies no deterministic polynomial-time circuit canonical form or identity algorithm that removes both costs.
open_obligations.attempted: The canonical PDAG algorithm eliminated path-dependent partition transport and gives linear delay in state outputs. Rational maps were represented by exact arithmetic circuits, their positive denominators were cleared, and expanded coefficient tables were used to decide global identity exactly. This closes correctness but not delay measured in distinct functional outputs.
open_obligations.partial_result: The state side is closed. The canonical PDAG algorithm enumerates every \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\) exactly once after \(O(p^3)\) initialization and with \(O(p+m)\) delay, and the unique formula for \(\mathsf L_C(H)\) proves transported partitions are path independent. Shortest certificates of length \(\delta(C,E)\) can be produced with the safe per-output bound \(O(p^5)\). For the effect side, \(\texttt{lem:exact-global-rational-effect-identity}\) proves a terminating deterministic exact test: clear the positive Gram-determinant denominators and expand every resulting numerator polynomial, whose coefficient table certifies global identity on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\). Enumerating all states and applying this test yields an exact finite partition and one representative per rational-functional class. The expansion and all-state traversal can be exponential in compact circuit size or in the number of distinct functionals, so this is not an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay solution to the narrowed question.

prose_updates.tldr: Equal incoming coefficients encode communities of direct causes. The published blocked edge-coloured class permits singleton blocks, whereas BPEC is its proper no-singleton subclass and is structurally identifiable. On the full singleton-permitting blocked class, equality of the full positive-definite covariance models is characterized exactly by common skeleton and unshielded colliders, common repeated parent blocks, and fixed orientation across unequal endpoint block families; equivalently, the states are connected by partition-compatible singleton covered reversals. The static class is also the set of consistent extensions of the ordinary CPDAG after inserting the background arrows \(F(C)\), with one canonical partition lift per extension. This yields exact-once enumeration after \(O(p^3)\) initialization and \(O(p+m)\) delay, a sharp \(p!\) component bound, generic fixed-\(p\) BIC component recovery, and simultaneous inference for the finite effect set. Deterministic output-sensitive quotienting by global rational identity of compact effect circuits remains open.

project_justification.fill: The project recovers repeated blocks from the identity tangent space, proves by an exact sparse regression separator that any reversed edge must join equal endpoint families, and combines these facts with monotone covered reversals to obtain the full static and transformational characterization. It then converts the static class to a canonical background PDAG: every repeated-block arrow is in \(F(C)\), every consistent extension has a unique path-independent partition lift, and the published linear-delay PDAG enumeration algorithm therefore enumerates the blocked component exactly once. The same quotient supports generic fixed-dimensional BIC recovery and simultaneous possible-effect inference, while exact output-sensitive rational-functional quotienting is isolated as a separate arithmetic-circuit problem.

prose_updates.related_work: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 is the writing and primary method anchor. Its Definition 5.14 defines blocked edge colourings without excluding singleton classes; properness is a separate condition, and BPEC is the blocked, proper no-singleton subclass. Its Theorem 5.17 proves structural identifiability within BPEC, while Question 5.19 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-coloured model equivalence. The present result agrees with that boundary on the BPEC subclass and gives a complete equivalence characterization on the published blocked superclass; it does not transfer a BPEC converse to arbitrary cross-target colourings. Chickering1995 supplies the disagreement-decreasing sequence of distinct covered reversals, while the tangent and separator arguments prove those reversals are legal for the coefficient partitions. WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023, Theorem 5, is used directly after forming the CPDAG-plus-\(F(C)\) PDAG: cubic Meek-closure initialization and linear-delay enumeration of consistent extensions carry over through the newly proved canonical partition-lift bijection. WienobstBannachLiskiewicz2023 addresses counting and sampling ordinary Markov classes, not rational effect-map quotienting. WuDrton2023 constrains innovation variances rather than incoming coefficients, and MakamReichenbachSeigal2023 studies likelihood geometry for a fixed compatibly coloured graph. Haughton1988 informs the finite smooth-model BIC argument. MaathuisKalischBuhlmann2009, ChangGuoMalinsky2026, and GuoPerkovic2022EfficientLS inform possible-effect estimation and inference but do not provide simultaneous inference over this full-model-equivalence component.
prose_updates.interpretation: Repeated coefficient blocks do two jobs. They survive every observationally equivalent representation, and each of their arrows becomes background knowledge because a parent contained in a repeated block cannot have the same block family as the target. After those arrows are fixed, the remaining graph uncertainty is precisely an ordinary Markov-equivalence extension problem, and the endpoint parent sets determine all residual singleton blocks uniquely. This orientation information is structural: an arrow compelled by the PDAG or by \(F(C)\) does not by itself identify its numerical coefficient.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The population component \(\mathcal R(C)\) is an equivalence class of complete covariance-model images, not the pointwise fibre of every state fitting one exceptional covariance. Zero edges and coincident coefficients can create additional pointwise representations outside the component. The fixed directed set \(F(C)\) records orientations forced directly by unequal nonsingleton families, while ordinary collider, acyclicity, and Meek-closure constraints can compel further arrows; neither kind of compelled arrow alone identifies a numerical coefficient. Canonical PDAG enumeration is linear-delay in state outputs, but the number of distinct rational effect maps can be much smaller than the number of states. Exact global rational identity is decidable by denominator clearing and coefficient expansion, yet no deterministic output-polynomial or polynomial-delay canonicalization bound for compact arithmetic circuits is claimed.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The equivalence theorem concerns finite labelled causally sufficient linear Gaussian DAGs, target-local coefficient blocks, unrestricted real block coefficients, unrestricted positive target-specific innovation variances, and full positive-definite covariance images. It does not cover cross-target edge colours, vertex-coloured innovation variances, latent confounding, selection, cycles, or pointwise supermodel fibres. State enumeration uses the canonical CPDAG-plus-\(F(C)\) PDAG and has \(O(p^3)\) initialization and \(O(p+m)\) delay after output-linear partition lifting; attaching a shortest legal-reversal certificate has the safe bound \(O(p^5)\) per output. The sharp state-count bound is \(p!\), attained by the complete all-singleton state. Exact quotienting of the emitted compact rational effect circuits is finite but not shown output-polynomial. The BIC and confidence results remain fixed-\(p\), pointwise, and generic away from a proper algebraic exceptional set; no greedy-search consistency or uniform inference near model intersections is asserted.
